title: Social Security Survivor Benefits: Who Qualifies and How Much
bigPicture: If you lose a spouse or parent who paid into Social Security, you may get monthly money to help you live.
whatYouNeedToKnow: Widows and widowers age 60 or older can get benefits. If disabled, it can start at age 50.
Children under 18 can get benefits. If still in high school, up to age 19. Disabled children may qualify at any age.
The amount is based on what the person earned while working. It is usually 75% to 100% of their full benefit.
You can get survivor benefits and your own retirement benefit, but Social Security pays the higher amount, not both full amounts.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Waiting too long to apply. Apply right away so you do not lose back payments.
Thinking remarriage ends your benefits. If you remarry after age 60, you still qualify.
Forgetting the $255 lump-sum death payment. Not everyone knows this is available.
actionSteps: Call Social Security at 1-800-772-1213 or visit ssa.gov to start your claim.
Gather your ID, the deceased person's SSN, and a copy of the death certificate.
Have your banking info ready so payments go straight to your account.
Ask about extra help like Medicare or SNAP if money is tight.
